radar_fcs.tooltip.fcs: Works with the equipment of its radar network: CBC mounts with aim controllers, Create Radars radars, monitors, memory blocks. Needs power (FE). RMB: settings and status, Shift+RMB: hold fire
radar_fcs.tooltip.transponder: IFF: right-click to set the code, the selection mode (sublevel, radius, or sublevel and distance) and the radius. Everything in the zone is friendly: mobs, players, vehicles, projectiles, ships. A fire control treats it as friendly if its code list (IFF tab) accepts the code. Needs power (FE). Dye only changes the colour
radar_fcs.report.radar_missing: no running radar on a link
radar_fcs.tooltip.monitor: Target screen fed by Create Radars radars of its radar network: friendly, hostile, inactive. RMB on a blip designates it for the network's fire controls (manual aiming), Shift+RMB opens the monitor window: target list, filters, scale. Build as a wall. Needs power (FE): 32 FE/t per screen block
radar_fcs.status.no_power: no rotation on the aim controller
radar_fcs.report.spread: [CBC spread ±%s°: longer barrel or fewer charges]
radar_fcs.gui.title: Fire Control Computer
radar_fcs.gui.fire_hint.single: One shot, then a pause. Fires only when the predicted miss is within tolerance. Pause in seconds; numbers change with the mouse wheel.
radar_fcs.gui.fire_hint.auto: Continuous fire while the predicted miss is within tolerance.
radar_fcs.gui.fire_hint.burst: A burst of the set length, then a pause. Counts projectiles that left the barrel. Pause in seconds; numbers change with the mouse wheel.
radar_fcs.gui.targets_hint: Sublevels are Sable / Create Aeronautics ships; entities are Create contraptions, boats, minecarts and the rest (shells and rockets: Intercept tab). Priority level: higher wins. Speed window per target type, in m/s, "off" means no limit. Numbers change with the mouse wheel.
radar_fcs.gui.drop_hint: A dropped target is ignored. Static means slower than the server minSpeed for longer than the standing time (a short stop such as a turn is not static yet; a target that never moved is static at once). After N shots - each gun counts its own shots and leaves the target after its N; saving settings brings dropped targets back.
radar_fcs.gui.pick_hint: Type level first, then the priority mode. Each mount picks on its own. Switching moves fire to another target and cycles through the left ones; with a single target fire continues. A target designated on the monitor goes first.
radar_fcs.tooltip.radar_link: Goes on equipment and adds it to a radar network, like a Stock Link. Placed untuned it starts a new network; RMB an existing link to tune to its network. Unlimited range, full redstone power disables it. Reset: Shift+RMB in air or in a crafting grid
radar_fcs.link.cleared: Cleared connection to the radar network
radar_fcs.link.not_linked: Link is not on a network
radar_fcs.tooltip.yaw_controller: Place directly under a CBC cannon mount and feed rotation from below. Turns the cannon horizontally by the needed angle; shaft speed sets the turn rate (256 RPM = 192°/s)
radar_fcs.tooltip.pitch_controller: Place directly beside a CBC cannon mount and feed rotation from the other side. Elevates the barrel by the needed angle; shaft speed sets the rate
radar_fcs.controller.no_mount_yaw: No mount: place it directly under a CBC cannon mount
radar_fcs.controller.no_mount_pitch: No mount: place it directly beside a CBC cannon mount
radar_fcs.link.place_on_equipment: A radar link goes on equipment: computer, CBC mount, radar or monitor
radar_fcs.link.tooltip_untuned: Not tuned: when placed it starts a new network. RMB an existing link to join its network
radar_fcs.link.disabled: Radar network %s: link disabled by redstone
radar_fcs.link.network_info: Radar network %s: fire controls %s, cannons %s, radars %s, monitors %s, memory %s, cameras %s, camera monitors %s
radar_fcs.gui.hostile_only: Mobs: hostile only (passive ones via the whitelist)
radar_fcs.gui.lists_hint: Entry: entity ID (minecraft:cow), type tag (#minecraft:undead), every entity of a mod (create:*) or the name of a player, ship or name-tagged entity. Whitelist: always a target, even if its type is off or the mob is passive; blacklist: never. Transponder friends and server limits override the lists.
radar_fcs.gui.assemble_hint: Assemble every cannon of this fire control now; afterwards it assembles them by itself again
radar_fcs.gui.disassemble_hint: Disassemble every cannon of this fire control (e.g. to rebuild it); it will not assemble them until "Assemble" is pressed
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.title: Radar Monitor
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.no_radar: No Create Radars radar in the monitor's network
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.coords: X %s Y %s Z %s, range %s m, height %s m, %s m/s
radar_fcs.gui.iff_mode_white: Mode: whitelist — only transponders with listed codes are friendly
radar_fcs.gui.iff_mode_black: Mode: blacklist — every transponder is friendly except listed codes
radar_fcs.gui.iff_hidden: Codes are hidden: only the fire control's owner, their team and operators see and change them.
radar_fcs.gui.iff_hint_white: Whitelist: a transponder is friendly only if its code is listed; transponders without a code or with other codes are hostile (protect nothing). Enter the code in the transponder too (right-click it). The owner, their team and friendlyPlayers are always friendly.
radar_fcs.gui.iff_hint_black: Blacklist: every transponder (also without a code) is friendly except the listed codes — their zones and ships are not protected. Enter the code in the transponder too (right-click it). The owner, their team and friendlyPlayers are always friendly.
radar_fcs.msg.transponder_locked: Someone else's transponder: only the owner, their team and operators see and change its settings
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.title: IFF Transponder
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.mode.sublevel: Selection: the sublevel it stands on
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_sublevel: Friendly: the whole Sable / Create Aeronautics ship (or Create contraption) the transponder stands on and everything within it: mobs, players, vehicles, projectiles.
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_sublevel_: The transponder is not on a sublevel: in this mode it protects nothing. Put it on a ship or choose "radius".
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_radius: Friendly: everything within the radius: mobs (hostile too), players, vehicles, contraptions, projectiles, ships. On a ship the ship itself is friendly too and the zone moves with it.
radar_fcs.tooltip.memory: In a fire control's radar network (via a link) adds %s more entries to each of its lists (target whitelist and blacklist, IFF codes). Needs power (FE)
radar_fcs.memory.on: Memory block online: +%s entries to the lists of the network's fire controls
radar_fcs.memory.off: No power: the memory block needs %s FE/t
radar_fcs.report.no_energy: NO POWER: the fire control needs %s FE/t
radar_fcs.report.memory: Memory: %s entries per list, memory blocks in the network: %s
radar_fcs.monitor.no_energy: No power: the monitor is off
radar_fcs.gui.list_no_memory: Inactive: not enough memory. Add a memory block to the network (+16 entries) or remove the entry
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.mode.sublevel_: Selection: sublevel and distance from it
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_combined: Friendly: the ship the transponder stands on and everything within the distance from its bounds: escorts, mobs, players, projectiles.
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_combined_: The transponder is not on a sublevel: in this mode it protects a sphere of the given radius around itself.
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.name: Name
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.inherit_hint: Entry: entity ID (minecraft:villager), tag (#minecraft:raiders), every entity of a mod (create:*) or the name of a player, ship or name-tagged entity. "Always" inherits protection even if its type is off; "never" does not. The ship carrying the transponder is always friendly.
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.scope_hint: Hover a blip for target details; click to designate it to the network's fire controls (manual aiming), click again to clear; middle-click excludes the target from fire, again restores it (also restored when it leaves radar coverage).
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.list_hint: Click: designate/clear; middle-click: exclude from fire/restore
radar_fcs.gui.impact_first: Same level: first the projectile that reaches us first
radar_fcs.gui.intercept_no_mod: CBC Interception is not installed on the server: projectiles are tracked but not shot down (without it CBC projectiles pass through each other).
radar_fcs.gui.intercept_hint.threatening: Hostile big cannon shells and rockets are shot down if their flight (CBC physics, until it hits blocks) passes closer than the threat radius to this computer, its cannons or friendly transponder zones. Friendly: fired by this computer's cannons, by computers of the same owner or team, or from friendly zones. Small ones (autocannons, machine guns, rocket pods) are not tracked.
radar_fcs.gui.intercept_hint.approaching: All hostile big cannon shells and rockets approaching this computer are shot down, even if they would miss. Friendly: fired by this computer's cannons, by computers of the same owner or team, or from friendly zones. Small ones (autocannons, machine guns, rocket pods) are not tracked.
radar_fcs.gui.intercept_hint.all: All hostile big cannon shells and rockets in reach are shot down wherever they fly. Friendly: fired by this computer's cannons, by computers of the same owner or team, or from friendly zones. Small ones (autocannons, machine guns, rocket pods) are not tracked.
radar_fcs.report.intercept_off: Interception: CBC Interception is not installed, projectiles are not shot down
radar_fcs.gui.wheel_hint: Mouse wheel: steps of 0.1 up to 1, then steps of 1; with Shift ten times more
radar_fcs.gui.mount_custom: Own targets for this cannon (otherwise the computer's common settings)
radar_fcs.gui.mounts_none: No cannons are linked to this computer (put a radar link on a mount).
radar_fcs.gui.mounts_hint_common: This cannon uses the computer's common target types and levels (Targets and Intercept tabs). Turn on own targets to set what it shoots at and what comes first: e.g. one autocannon only shoots down shells, another hits mobs.
radar_fcs.gui.mounts_hint_own: Own target types and levels of this cannon. The rest is common: white and black lists (whitelist bypasses types), speed windows, IFF, threat filter, fire mode, drop and pick rules. A target designated on a monitor goes to all cannons.
radar_fcs.msg.excluded: Target excluded from fire: %s (middle-click again to restore)
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.pins_empty: No markers. Right-click the map on the Screen tab to place one.
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.pins_hint: Right-click the map to place a marker, right-click a marker to remove it. Markers are visual only and do not affect fire.
radar_fcs.link.overflow: Radar network %s is full: %s links for %s allowed - this one is inactive (each powered memory block adds 16)
radar_fcs.link.usage: Network connections: %s of %s (16 + 16 per memory block)
radar_fcs.tooltip.camera: Goes on a wall, ceiling or floor. Joins a radar network with a radar link or without one: right-click a radar link with the camera to tune it, like a Create factory gauge. From a camera monitor of the network you can look through it and aim the guns by its view.
radar_fcs.tooltip.camera_monitor: Right-click: cameras of its radar network - pick one and look through it. LMB - fire signal to all guns of the network (like redstone 15, hold - continuous), Shift - exit. Energy: 64 FE/t per camera in the network.
radar_fcs.camera.not_linked: This camera is not in the monitor's radar network
radar_fcs.camera.busy: Another player is controlling this camera
radar_fcs.camera.hint: LMB - fire signal to all guns of the network (hold - continuous), Shift - exit
radar_fcs.camera_gui.title: Camera Monitor
radar_fcs.camera_gui.empty: There are no cameras in this monitor's radar network. Place a camera and connect it to the monitor with radar links.
radar_fcs.camera_gui.hint: Camera name - Enter saves. "Guns" - which guns the camera controls (all by default); while you look through it, their auto-aim is paused.
radar_fcs.status.camera_self: camera is looking at the gun itself: holding still
radar_fcs.tooltip.gun_rotator: Requires Sable (Create Aeronautics). Power with a shaft at the back. Right-click with an empty hand to assemble the structure in front (glue rules like a bearing) into a hinged rotating part. The fire control computer sets its angle through a gun link and a sight.
radar_fcs.rotator.no_sable: The gun rotator needs Sable (Create Aeronautics)
radar_fcs.rotator.nothing: Nothing to assemble in front of the rotator
radar_fcs.rotator.not_assembled: Not assembled: right-click with an empty hand
radar_fcs.tooltip.sight: Placed with the lens facing where you look. Marks which direction of the gun to aim at the target; surrounding blocks don't matter. Without a sight the barrel of the gun's CBC mount is aimed. Outputs a redstone signal while the gun should fire (also with CBC mounts).
radar_fcs.tooltip.gun_link: Joins the parts of one gun - sight, rotators, drives and CBC mounts - into a gun network. Shift+right-click: gun settings (name, type, auto-aim, firing). Put the radar link on any part of the gun.
radar_fcs.sight.info: Sight: heading %s°, elevation %s°; rotators and drives %s, CBC mounts %s
radar_fcs.sight.no_rotators: No rotators or drives: connect the sight to them with gun links
radar_fcs.gun_link.info: Gun %s: sights %s, rotators and drives %s, CBC mounts %s
radar_fcs.gun_link.no_sight: The gun has neither a sight nor a CBC mount - the computer does not know what to aim
radar_fcs.gun_link.place_on_gun: A gun link goes on a sight, a gun rotator or drive, or a CBC mount
radar_fcs.status.turret_no_power: no rotation on a gun rotator or drive
radar_fcs.status.turret_no_rotator: gun has no rotators or drives
radar_fcs.tooltip.gun_drive: Like a gearshift: input shaft at the back, output shaft at the front, but the output speed (-100% to 100% of the input) is set by the fire control. Drives anything: the bearing of a turning part, the yaw or pitch shaft of a CBC mount. Right-click with an empty hand: yaw or pitch mode. Joins the gun with a gun link.
radar_fcs.camera_monitor.no_energy: Camera monitor lacks energy: needs %s FE/t (64 per camera)
radar_fcs.gun.title: Gun
radar_fcs.gun.name: Name
radar_fcs.gun.type.autocannon.hint: CBC autocannon ballistics; the fire signal is held while the gun is on target. With a CBC mount in the gun, ballistics and firing follow the mount.
radar_fcs.gun.type.medium.hint: Ballistics between autocannon and big cannon; fires in pulses. With a CBC mount in the gun, ballistics and firing follow the mount.
radar_fcs.gun.type.big.hint: CBC big cannon ballistics; fires in pulses (signal edge). With a CBC mount in the gun, ballistics and firing follow the mount.
radar_fcs.gun.type.custom.hint: Your own weapon: aims straight at the target, without lead or ballistics; the signal is held while on target.
radar_fcs.camera.tuned: Camera tuned to radar network %s - place it, no link needed
radar_fcs.camera.tooltip_untuned: Right-click a radar link to tune it to that network (no link needed for the camera)
radar_fcs.camera_gui.guns_empty: No fire controls with cannons or guns in this monitor's network.
radar_fcs.camera_gui.guns_hint: Checked guns aim by this camera's view and fire on LMB; the others keep engaging targets on their own. Nothing checked - all guns. * - a gun on rotators or drives.
radar_fcs.ponder.tag.fire_control.descri: Fire control computer, links, aim controllers, monitors, cameras and guns
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.header: A battery: computer, cannon and radar
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_1: The Fire Control Computer aims Create Big Cannons and fires on its own. The cannon sits on a CBC mount or a compact mount from CBC: Firepower Components; big cannons, autocannons and addon guns all work
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_2: The mount needs aim controllers: yaw below it, pitch on its side. Feed rotation into the controllers, not the mount: shaft speed sets how fast the cannon turns
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_3: Targets come from Create: Radars radars: plane radar, radar bearing and others. Without a working radar in the network there is no fire (except a manually designated target)
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_4: The computer can stand anywhere. It needs 1024 FE/t of electricity; without power it sees no targets
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_5: Everything connects with Radar Links of one network, like Create Stock Links. Distance does not matter
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_6: The computer picks a target, leads it with CBC ballistics (charges, barrels, shell), turns the cannon and fires. Each shot refines the ballistics
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_7: It fires only when a shot from the current barrel position will hit and no friends or blocks are in the way
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_8: Right-click the computer for settings (see the next scene). Shift+right-click holds or allows fire; aiming continues
radar_fcs.ponder.computer_settings.text_: Right-click the computer to open its settings. Each computer has its own, stored in the block. Change numbers with the mouse wheel or the -/+ buttons (Shift for bigger steps)
Fire tab: fire mode. Single: one shot, then a pause. Automatic: fire while the shot will hit. Burst: N shots, then a pause in seconds. Shots are counted by projectiles leaving the barrel
Targets tab: what to engage: ships, players, mobs, entities (boats, minecarts, contraptions). Each type has a priority level 1-5 (higher first) and a speed window "from ... to ..." m/s

Lists tab: the whitelist is always engaged, regardless of types; the blacklist never. Entries: an id (minecraft:zombie), a tag (#minecraft:undead), a whole mod (create:*) or a player, ship or name-tagged mob name. 16 entries + 16 per Memory Block

Drop tab: when to give up a target: static ones (standing longer than the "standing time"; a short stop does not count), moving ones, or after N shots - each gun fires its own N shots. Saving the settings restores dropped targets

Pick tab: which target comes first: nearest, earliest, farthest, largest, smallest, fastest or slowest. "Switch to a higher priority target" and the switching rule: after N shots, after a time, when it stops, or never
IFF tab: a whitelist or blacklist of transponder codes - which transponders count as friendly
Intercept tab: shoot down big cannon shells and rockets (needs the CBC Interception mod). Threat filter: threatening (landing near friends), approaching or all hostile; "earlier impact first"
Guns tab: targets for a single gun - which types and levels it engages, e.g. one gun for ships, another for mobs
Status tab: a summary of radars, guns and their status, miss and barrel spread, targets. The "Assemble cannons" and "Disassemble cannons" buttons help with reloading and rebuilding
Shift+right-click holds or allows fire. Create's Engineer's Goggles show the same summary, a Display Link has a "Fire control targets" source, a comparator reads the target count
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_1: The Yaw Controller goes right below the mount (above a hanging one). Its shaft comes in from below
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_2: The Pitch Controller goes on the side of the mount, with its shaft on the far side
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_3: The controller turns the cannon by exactly the commanded angle. Speed works like CBC shafts: 0.0375° per tick for each RPM
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_4: 256 RPM gives 9.6° per tick (192° per second), 64 RPM gives 2.4°. For fast targets use 128-256 RPM
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_5: Load: 4 stress units per RPM. While the computer controls the mount, its own shafts are locked. The output half-shaft shows the cannon angle
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_6: Without a controller ("no aim controller") or rotation the cannon neither aims nor fires. Engineer's Goggles show the turn speed
radar_fcs.ponder.network.header: Radar networks and the Memory Block
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_1: Computers, mounts, radars, monitors, cameras and gun parts connect only through Radar Links; nothing connects by range on its own
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_2: Place a link on a device. An untuned link starts a new radar network (its name, like "#3F2A", appears in chat)
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_3: Right-click a placed link with a link item to tune the item to its network; it glows. Next links join that network
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_4: All devices of one network are connected at any distance within a dimension. Looking at a link highlights its network
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_5: Right-clicking a link and Engineer's Goggles show the network name and how many computers, guns, radars and monitors it has. A device can join several networks with links on different faces
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_6: A network holds 16 device links plus 16 per powered Memory Block (240 FE/t). Each Memory Block also adds 16 entries to every list of the computer. Extra links report "network full"
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_7: A redstone signal of strength 15 disables a link; remove the signal to bring it back
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_8: Shift+right-click in the air or the crafting grid resets the link item
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_1: Place monitors as a wall up to 6x6: it forms a single screen
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_2: Put a link on any screen block. The monitor draws a map of targets and radars of its network: the monitor is in the center, up points away from you, "N" marks north
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_3: On the map: friendly, threat, peaceful and inactive targets in different colors, targets under fire, radar beams and zones, transponders and range marks on the axes
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_4: Shift+right-click opens the monitor window. The Screen tab shows the same map: click a target to designate it, type the map size (16 - 1,000,000 blocks)
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_5: Computers of the network engage a designated target first, ignoring types and speed. The Targets tab lists targets to designate or clear
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_6: The View tab: display filters (friendly, threats, peaceful, inactive, radars, zones, transponders, pins), icons for each type - shape, color, size - and name labels: always or on hover
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_7: Pins: right-click the map in the window or use the Pins tab: coordinates, name and color. Pins are only drawn and do not affect fire
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_8: In the world: looking at a target shows its details, a middle-click excludes it from the computers (again to restore)
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_9: Power: 32 FE/t per screen block, fed into any block of the wall
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_1: The transponder marks friends: computers do not fire at anything in its zone or through it
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_2: Right-click opens the transponder screen. The name (up to 32 characters) labels the target and its monitor mark. The code (1-8 digits) tells computers whether it is friendly
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_3: Radius mode: a sphere of the set radius around the transponder; on a ship the zone moves with it
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_4: Sub-level mode: the Sable ship or contraption it stands on (bounds + 2 blocks); "sub-level and distance": the ship plus a set distance around. The default depends on where it stands
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_5: The Inheritance tab sets who in the zone is protected: players, hostile and peaceful mobs, ships, contraptions, projectiles, others. "Always" and "never" lists work like the computer target lists
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_6: The computer IFF tab holds a whitelist or blacklist of codes - which transponders are friendly
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_7: Only the owner, their team and operators see and change codes. Power: 64 FE/t; without it the transponder protects nothing
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_1: A camera goes on a wall, ceiling or floor. Its head turns where you look through it and keeps its last position
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_2: Connect it with a Radar Link or without one: right-click a Radar Link (or a networked camera) with the camera item to tune it. Shift+right-click in the air resets it
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_3: The Camera Monitor (right-click) lists the cameras of its network. Rename a camera with Enter; "View" looks from the camera center
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_4: While you look, auto aim of the network guns pauses: they aim where the camera looks, up to 384 blocks, leading moving ships and entities
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_5: Left-click fires all controlled guns like redstone 15 (hold for continuous fire). Shift exits
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_6: The "Guns" button in a camera row chooses which guns it controls. The others keep tracking targets or follow another camera. Nothing checked means all guns
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_7: Looking at a controlled gun itself (or, from a camera mounted on it, at its own parts) keeps it still; left-click still fires
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_8: The monitor uses 64 FE/t per camera in its network. Walk away or exit and the guns go back to auto aim at once
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.header: A custom gun on Swivel Bearings
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_1: A custom Sable gun is built on Create Aeronautics Swivel Bearings. Yaw: a bearing facing up
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_2: The bearing is driven through its cog. A Gun Drive in yaw mode feeds it through cogwheels; the computer sets the drive output speed and direction
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_3: Select the rotating part with Super Glue. The bearing assembles it into a Sable structure once its cog gets rotation
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_4: On the rotating part goes a second bearing facing sideways for pitch. Glue its rotating part (the barrel) too; assemble the inner bearing first
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_5: A second drive turns the pitch bearing: right-click it with an empty hand for pitch mode. Rotation can reach the rotating part through a shaft passing through the yaw bearing
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_6: The barrel can be any blocks. Place the Sight facing along the barrel: the computer aims the sight direction, so the shape does not matter
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_7: Gun Links on the drives and the sight join them into one gun (an untuned link starts a new gun, right-click a placed one to tune the item)
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_8: Put a Radar Link on any part of the gun: one link connects the whole gun. The gun's own structure is neither a target nor an obstacle
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_9: The computer learns the drive ratio and direction from how the sight turns; if aiming wobbles at first, it settles within seconds
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_10: When it is time to fire, the sight emits redstone 15 - wire it to your weapon. CBC mounts in the gun fire on command by themselves
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_11: Shift+right-click a Gun Link for gun settings. For a custom weapon pick its type: autocannon, medium, big (ballistics and signal kind) or "custom" - aims straight at the target without lead
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_rotator.text_1: The Gun Rotator (needs Sable) is the mod's own bearing: it turns the structure in front of its output. Feed rotation from behind; turn speed works like aim controllers
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_rotator.text_2: Right-click with an empty hand to assemble (Create glue rules), again to show the angle. Layout: a horizontal rotator carrying a vertical one. Assemble the inner one first
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_rotator.text_3: Place the Sight facing along the barrel: the computer aims the sight direction
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_rotator.text_4: Gun Links join the sight and rotators into one gun; a Radar Link on any part connects it to the computer
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_rotator.text_5: The rotator holds its angle itself. With Create Aeronautics you can also build on Swivel Bearings with Gun Drives - see the "custom gun on Swivel Bearings" scene
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_1: The Gun Drive works like a gearbox: input behind, output in front (-100% to 100% of input). The computer sets the output. Here it turns the yaw shaft of the mount instead of an aim controller
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_2: Right-click with an empty hand to switch the drive between yaw (↔) and pitch (↕)
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_3: The output can drive a bearing, gears or a mount shaft. The computer learns the ratio and direction by itself
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_4: Gun Links join drives, mounts and sights into one gun
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_5: Shift+right-click a Gun Link for gun settings (shared by all its links). The name shows in the computer report and the camera monitor
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_6: The type sets ballistics and the signal for guns without a CBC mount: autocannon - the signal holds while on target; medium and big - pulses; custom - aims straight at the target without lead. With a CBC mount, ballistics come from it
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_7: Auto aim off: the gun aims only from a camera. Firing off: the gun aims but never fires by itself (camera left-click still works)
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_8: A link on a CBC mount also has "Main cannon": its barrel is aimed when the gun has no sight, and its ballistics are used
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_9: The CBC mount of the gun fires on command; the computer does not lock its shafts. Put a Radar Link on any part of the gun
